title: An alcohol-solution combustion combining with gel calcination process for the preparation of Ni<sub>x</sub>Co<sub>y</sub>Cu<sub>(1-x-y)</sub>Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> magnetic nanoparticles and their adsorption performances of Congo red from aqueous solution
content:
by Yidong Xie, Zhenghui Ge, Zhou Wang, Zhan-ao Wu

NixCoyCu(1-x-y)Fe2O4 magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) were successfully prepared through a novel and economical strategy coupling alcohol solution combustion with gel calcination, and their physicochemical and magnetic performances were verified by XRD, TEM and VSM techniques. For larger specific surface area and saturation magnetization to apply, three key elements those affected the whole preparation process including element proportion, calcination temperature, and absolute alcohol amount, and different characterization technique were optimized, and for the adsorption of Congo red (CR) dye, Ni0.1Co0.8Cu0.1Fe2O4 MNPs were fabricated under the conditions of 400 °C calcination for 2 hours with 65 mL absolute alcohol, the obtained product exhibited a uniform particle size of 18.9 nm and a saturation magnetization value of 76.4 emu/g. The influencing factors on the adsorption, including adsorption time, concentration of CR solution, and pH, were systematically investigated, and the adsorption mechanism was revealed, further analysis revealed that the adsorption process for CR on the nanoparticles exhibited a high consistency with pseudo-second-order kinetic and Langmuir models, which revealed that the adsorption of CR on Ni0.1Co0.8Cu0.1Fe2O4 MNPs belonged to the single-layer chemisorption, the adsorption efficiency remained at 81.4% of their first adsorption even after undergoing 8 cycles, and the adsorption capacity maintained larger values when the pH of CR solution was not more than 9.
author: Yidong Xie
